newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cabinet approves annual economic report.
newsitem.headline: German cabinet approves annual economic report.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet on Tuesday rubber-stamped a government report which predicts more jobless and a budget deficit just below the qualifying limit for European monetary union (EMU).
The annual economic report, to be presented shortly by Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt, foresees economic growth this year of 2.5 percent, up from 1.4 percent in 1996.

It also expects unemployment to climb to 11 percent from 10.3 percent, putting pressure on Finance Minister Theo Waigel to meet his goal of reducing the deficit below the Maastricht ceiling of three percent of gross domestic product.
The report forecasts a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of GDP - up from the 2.5 percent assumption on which Waigel's 1997 budget was based.

Germany has insisted on strict adherence to the Maastricht criteria this year -- judgement year for the EMU "ins" and "outs" -- to try and ensure the euro currency is not watered down by weaker European currencies after its launch in 1999.
